title: CodeStorm 2026: FutureForge
description: CodeStorm 2026: FutureForge is a student-focused innovation hackathon where developers, designers, creators, and problem-solvers come together to build impactful solutions using technology. Unlike traditional hackathons that focus on a single domain, FutureForge embraces Open Innovation , allowing participants to tackle real-world challenges across any field they are passionate about. Whether it's Artificial Intelligence, Web Development, Cybersecurity, Education Technology, Sustainability, Productivity Tools, Mobile Applications, or something entirely unique, this is your platform to innovate. This hackathon is part of the CodeStorm 2026 Series , an initiative dedicated to empowering students through hands-on learning, collaboration, and innovation. The event will be conducted completely online through our Discord community. Participation is free, and teams may consist of 1–6 members . Participants are encouraged to think boldly, experiment fearlessly, and build projects that create meaningful impact while showcasing technical excellence and creativity. CodeStorm is a student-led initiative dedicated to creating opportunities for young innovators, builders, and creators across India. title: Beginner's Paradise - FirstCommit
description: Submission Requirements To complete your submission, each team or individual must submit the following on Devpost before the deadline: Required A working project created during the hackathon. A public GitHub repository containing your source code. A project description explaining what you built, how it works, and the problem it solves. A demo video (3–5 minutes) showcasing your project and its main features. Clear setup instructions (README) so judges can run your project if necessary. Recommended A live deployment or hosted version of your project. Screenshots or images of your project. A list of technologies, frameworks, APIs, or libraries used. Any presentation slides or additional documentation. Rules Your project should be started during the hackathon. Existing libraries, templates, and frameworks are allowed, but the core work must be completed during the event. Projects may be built individually or in teams (within the allowed team size). You must own or have permission to use all assets included in your submission. AI tools may be used unless a specific prize category states otherwise. Please disclose any significant AI assistance in your project description. Incomplete, non-functional, or plagiarized submissions may be disqualified. Most importantly, don't worry if your project isn't perfect. First Commit is about learning, building, and taking the next step in your development journey.

title: OpenCV AI Competition 2026, powered by AWS
description: About The Competition • Competition launch, registration, and proposal submission—runs August 12- 2026; proposals are accepted starting August 13. • 50 teams will be selected to receive a cloud compute grant valued at $150. All other teams, including those that submit the cloud compute grant proposal remain eligible to continue to the two-month build phase. Apply for your grant here. • Final projects are due October 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. • Every entry must use OpenCV 5 for substantive image or video analysis and run a meaningful component on AWS. • Two optional featured paths offer separate $1,000 awards: the Best Use of COOL Award and the Agentic Vision Award. Sponsor: Amazon Web Services (“Amazon” or “Sponsor”) Administrator: OpenCV Foundation (OpenCV or Administrator, and together with Amazon, the “organizers”) Join, Build, and Win Turn an ambitious idea into a working vision application, demonstrate measurable value, and share it with the global OpenCV community. The competition emphasizes Physical AI and Generative AI systems in which visual understanding drives useful decisions, actions, predictions, or interactions. Entries may pursue either featured path below, combine both, or take another approach and remain fully eligible to win a prize.. Projects may use any programming language or supporting hardware, provided they meet the core OpenCV 5 and AWS requirements on this page. Build Phase — Two Months From August 26 through October 26, all teams that submitted the required proposal will build, evaluate, document, and submit their final projects. • Teams are encouraged to join the official Slack channel to collaborate with others, and to use the #OpenCVComp26 hashtag on social media to share progress and milestones. • Teams who received a cloud compute grant must complete one 30-minute Zoom check-in with an organizing committee member during September 21–October 2 to receive the other 50% of their grant. • Teams must maintain active development and provide a concise progress update at the check-in. • Final submissions are due on October 26 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. Final Judging and Winners Final judging will take place from October 27 through November 9. Winners are scheduled to be announced on November 10 during an OpenCV Live! webinar or another announced OpenCV channel. What AWS Grant Proposals Must Include Each proposal must include: A team name A clear problem statement and intended real-world impact. The planned OpenCV 5 image or video analysis. The planned AWS architecture and services. A high-level architecture diagram or technical description. The target users or beneficiaries. The proposed evaluation method and judge demonstration. Whether the team intends to pursue the COOL path, the Agentic Vision path, both, or neither. Team Bio: A short team bio of all team members and their participation in any hackathons or competitions. Team strength will be used to judge the recipients of the cloud compute grant. Apply For an AWS Compute Grant Here Free AWS Credits for New Members New AWS customers are eligible to receive $100 in AWS Free Tier credits when they sign up for a Free Plan account and may earn up to $100 more through eligible activities. Teams may use these credits for eligible AWS services in this competition, subject to current AWS Free Tier terms , service availability, and expiration rules. Use of the Free Tier Credits is subject to the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions . AWS Promotional Credits are not redeemable for cash and can only be applied to AWS Services.

title: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
description: Welcome to the Amazon Developer Hackathon For the first time, Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all part of one global hackathon. Build for one product or use several to connect the living room, the front door, and the cloud. Get started now with our SDKs, simulators, and sample code. New to building for Amazon devices and services? We'll help you get from idea to submission with documentation and live office hours. Use our AI tools to prototype and troubleshoot along the way. Choose a track and show off what you build! 🚀 Why join? Be part of the first hackathon where Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all open to outside developers at once Your product feedback goes directly to the teams building Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee Compete for a share of $190K value of cash and AWS credits, plus a 1:1 meeting with the Amazon Developer team for track winners Get Started Pick your track: Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee, or Ring Set up the developer environment for your track (see Resources ) Review the track details and requirements to start building Submit your working demo, code repo, and product feedback by the deadline

title: Global Innovation Build Challenge V2
description: About the challenge Getting code to run has never been easier. Getting a system to actually work, at scale, under real constraints, is still hard. That gap is what this hackathon is about. Global Innovation Build Challenge (GIBC) V2 is a fully online, student-led international hackathon. GIBC V1 brought together 552 participants worldwide with backing from sponsors including NordVPN. V2 builds on that with three tracks, an international judging panel, and a larger sponsor lineup. Over the 10-week build period from July 11 to October 1, 2026 , you can register at any time, build solo or in a team of up to 6, and submit to one of three tracks. Projects are reviewed by a panel of industry professionals and academic experts, with winners announced at a virtual closing ceremony on October 8, 2026 . Track 01: TECH (Foundational LLM Development) Build and train a language model capped at 50 million parameters. You design the architecture, curate the data, and write the training loop. We want to see how much capability you can pull out of a deliberately small model. See the Rules page for exactly what the 50M cap includes and which benchmarks we score on. Example directions: a domain-specific assistant for legal or cryptographic text; a model optimized for on-device inference; a small generative model trained on a narrow technical corpus without touching a commercial API. Track 02: Applied (Medical Technology & Finance) Build a data-driven system on real, empirical datasets that solves a problem in healthcare or finance. This means predictive models, diagnostic pipelines, or automated financial systems, backed by data engineering that turns raw input into something a person could actually act on. Example directions: diagnostic software that processes device telemetry; analytics pipelines for pharmaceutical research; quantitative trading models driven by market indicators; automated risk scoring or fraud detection. All datasets must be public or de-identified, and prototypes must not be deployed on real patients or real money. See the Rules page. Track 03: Open (General Technical Invention) Build a functional prototype that shows technical novelty and cross-disciplinary engineering. Software, hardware, interactive media, generative systems, or any combination. No architectural limits and no resource constraints. Example directions: IoT-connected physical infrastructure; a tool that changes how you work day to day; a generative AI product; a full-stack application aimed at an environmental or community problem. Get started 1. Register on Devpost (July 11 to October 1) Sign up here on Devpost. You must be registered on Devpost to submit, even if you signed up on our website first. 2. Build solo or form a team (1 to 6 members) Work alone or assemble a team of up to 6. Once your team is set, pick the one track that fits what you want to build. Each team submits one project to one track. 3. Join the Discord (recommended) Join the official GIBC V2 Discord to find teammates, ask the organizers questions, and get announcements: https://discord.gg/4y6RghaSt5 4. Submit before the deadline (October 1, 11:45pm GMT+8) Submit all six required components on Devpost before the deadline. Late submissions are not reviewed.

title: RevenueCat Shipaton 2026
description: Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $740,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $740,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. NEW: Shipaton Demo Day in Times Square. Every category winner who comes to New York will have the opportunity to demo their app to the public, meet potential users, and gather candid feedback beneath the winners’ Times Square billboards. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Times Square Demo Day for category winners Every Shipaton category winner who attends in person will have the opportunity to demo their winning app at Shipaton Demo Day in Times Square on October 22, 2026. Builders will rotate through shared demo pods between 10 AM and 6 PM. Participation is optional and subject to scheduling. Travel is included only for prizes that expressly list travel. Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping!

title: Innosprint2.0
description: Welcome to the epicentre of innovation and collaboration – the D4 Community's Hackathon at CGC Jhanjeri! What We Are: D4 Community is proud to present an exhilarating hackathon hosted at CGC Jhanjeri, where we bring together budding tech enthusiasts, aspiring innovators, and problem solvers under one roof. With a passion for technology and a drive for innovation, we're dedicated to fostering an environment where bright minds can thrive. Our Mission: Our mission is simple yet profound: to challenge participants to harness their creativity, coding skills, and teamwork to solve real-world problems. We believe in the transformative power of collaboration and coding, and we aim to inspire the next generation of tech leaders. What to Expect: Expect an adrenaline-fueled 24 hours of non-stop coding, brainstorming, and networking. Participants will tackle exciting challenges, engage in workshops, and have the opportunity to win fantastic prizes. HealthTech Innovation : Dive into the world of healthcare and wellness by developing solutions that can improve medical services, patient care, or health monitoring. EdTech Revolution : Revolutionize education with technology. Create tools and platforms that enhance the learning experience, making education more accessible and engaging. Smart Cities and IoT : Innovate for the future of urban living. Build IoT solutions that can make cities smarter, more efficient, and better connected. Agriculture and AgriTech : Explore innovations in agriculture. Build tools or systems that can improve crop yield, farm management, or address food security challenges. Blockchain and Cryptocurrency : Dive into the world of blockchain technology and cryptocurrencies. Work on projects related to decentralized finance (DeFi), NFTs (Non-Fungible Tokens), or blockchain-based voting systems. Robotics and Automation : Explore the possibilities of robotics and automation. Build robots or automated systems that can assist in various industries, from manufacturing to healthcare. E-Commerce Enhancement : Explore ways to enhance the e-commerce experience. Develop solutions for better online shopping, personalized recommendations, or streamlined supply chain management. Open Theme : Don't see a theme that fits your idea? No problem! You're welcome to participate with any tech-related project that excites you. Why Join Us: Join us to broaden your horizons, sharpen your skills, and make lifelong connections with like-minded individuals. Whether you're a seasoned coder or just getting started, the D4 Community's Hackathon at CGC Jhanjeri is the place to be. Stay Tuned: Stay tuned for updates, registration details, and exciting announcements as we gear up for an unforgettable hackathon experience. Together, let's push the boundaries of innovation and make a positive impact on the world through technology. title: OneAquaHealth IEEE Global Hackathon
description: About the challenge ***At this stage, the judging panel has been carefully selected and finalized, and we are not seeking additional judges**** Please register to receive regular updates and access upcoming sessions listed under the Rules section, which are essential for building a successful project. ** Registration Still Open** Register and Start Building Recordings from all previous sessions are available here: https://www.oneaquahealth.eu/project-events/ These sessions cover the key concepts, resources, expectations, and guidance participants need for the hackathon, including what we are looking for in strong submissions. We highly encourage participants to review the recordings as they develop and finalize their solutions. For complete session schedules and participation details, please visit the Rules section. The IEEE OneAquaHealth Global Hackathon 2026 focuses on improving the sustainability and health of urban freshwater ecosystems by combining technology, citizen science, and the One Health approach. Urban aquatic environments are critical to biodiversity and human well-being but face increasing challenges due to urbanization, climate change, and limited monitoring capabilities. This challenge invites participants to build solutions that empower citizens and communities to actively contribute to environmental monitoring through intuitive tools and engaging experiences. Teams will explore ways to transform citizen-generated and environmental data into actionable insights that support researchers, policymakers, and local communities in making informed decisions. Participants are encouraged to leverage AI, data platforms, and digital health standards to improve the accuracy, reliability, and interoperability of ecosystem data while maintaining a human-centered approach. The hackathon also emphasizes raising awareness, fostering community engagement, and promoting long-term stewardship of urban water ecosystems through storytelling, gamification, and participatory design. By integrating environmental, climate, and citizen data, teams will help build early-warning systems, resilience tools, and decision-support platforms that strengthen ecosystem sustainability. Ultimately, this hackathon aims to advance the OneAquaHealth mission of connecting ecosystem health, biodiversity, and human well-being , driving innovation toward healthier communities and a more sustainable future. The hackathon aligns closely with the OneAquaHealth project, which is funded by the European Union. OneAquaHealth connects ecosystem health and human well-being through innovative tools for early detection of environmental risks. By combining biodiversity indicators, digital monitoring technologies, and community participation, OneAquaHealth helps identify how urban aquatic ecosystems respond to stressors. This holistic One Health approach supports evidence-based decisions for healthier, more resilient cities. Get started Register on Devpost before the deadline Form a team or participate individually Choose a track aligned with your interests Understand the problem and define your impact Build a prototype using AI, data, or citizen science approaches Follow OneAquaHealth project on LinkedIn , X and Facebook to make hackathon announcements, engage with the community in Europe and receive ideas that may support your project. Join the OneAquaHealth Community to connect with researchers, innovators, and citizen scientists and access domain knowledge relevant to your hackathon solution. Download and use the OneAquaHealth Citizen Science App to explore real environmental data, contribute your own observations, and gain hands ‑ on experience with the types of inputs your hackathon prototype may build upon. Join sessions & mentorship for guidance Submit your project with demo, code, and description 🌱 Tip Focus on building solutions that are impactful, practical, and scalable .

title: AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS) Agentic AI Partner Hackathon
description: Calling all AWS Partners! We are inviting you to build the next wave of conversational solutions on AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS)! AWS CDS enables AWS Partners to help customers engage users at a global scale through AWS End User Messaging (EUM) which includes Rich Communication Services (RCS), Short Message Services (SMS), and WhatsApp. It also includes Amazon Simple Email Service (SES). AWS CDS is the infrastructure that powers messaging across Amazon.com , Amazon Cognito, SNS, and Amazon Connect. AWS CDS is often used for one-time passwords (OTP), notifications, and rules-based chatbots that follow rigid scripts. We challenge you to think beyond this. The future of customer engagement is conversational: reaching customers in the channel (i.e. email vs. RCS vs. WhatsApp) they prefer, picking up right where the last conversation left off, and using two-way communication so customers tell you directly what they want and share signals that improve your products and services. Picture omnichannel experiences where a conversation starts in one channel and completes an action in another: a prescription refill reminder via SMS that lets the patient find and schedule the nearest pharmacy pickup through RCS with a tap, then sends dosage instructions via email, all without leaving the messaging experience. Push the boundaries. Build agentic solutions where AWS CDS is the communications backbone, powered by AI such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Surprise us with your real customer and industry solutions! Why You Should Participate Innovate with AWS CDS . Get hands-on with AWS CDS combined with agentic AI powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Solve Real Customer Problems . Create agentic solutions tied to customer and industry use cases that can scale across your customer base. Package your hackathon submission into a repeatable offering, list it on AWS Marketplace, and win AWS Specialist GTM and enablement support to accelerate real customer deals. Win Big . Compete for your share of $40,000 USD in cash prizes, in addition to an opportunity for a joint case study and 1:1 access to AWS Specialists to build and grow your AWS CDS practice and hackathon solution. Visibility for Your Organization . Winners will be announced via Devpost and the top winner will be offered a joint case study with AWS. Drive awareness and new leads to your practice. Direct Access to AWS Specialists . Join live webinars and weekly office hours to ask questions, get feedback, and shape the services roadmap. How to Get Started Now Brainstorm Your Idea . Think outside the box to improve customer communication experience through AWS CDS. Review the Tech Stack . Familiarize yourself with the AWS CDS services and how to pair them with agentic AI frameworks such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See the Requirements below. Form Your Team (Optional). Find collaborators within the same AWS Partner organization who are excited to improve customer problems through AWS CDS. Diverse skillsets in development, architecture, and customer engagement can go a long way. Start Building . Stand up an RCS agent within 5 minutes to develop an entire solution, decide later to use RCS or phone numbers for each country you’re serving, and expand from there.

title: Build With AI: Basics
description: Build With AI: Basics Build a working first draft of an app in an afternoon using AI best practices, with a set of reusable skills in your coding agent. Learn with a live build session, office hours, community, and a $2,500 prize pool, while creating something useful to your work or your life. About the challenge Devpost has launched a new kind of hackathon: shorter, built around learning, and open to join every month. Have you ever asked an AI to help you code something, only to watch it repeat a mistake you already fixed, forget a decision you made ten prompts ago, or hand back code that "works" but you can't explain? It happens to almost everyone who starts building with AI. Nobody showed you the basics. This hackathon does. You'll build a proof of concept: a small app that runs and does one thing end to end. To get there, you'll install the Devpost Learn Skill Pack , step-by-step guides that live inside your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any agent that supports skills). The skills interview you about your idea, help you plan it before any code gets written, build it with you, and get it ready to submit. You'll finish with a running app, the plan that got you there, and a habit you can reuse on every project after this one. Why join Learn to plan before you build, by letting the AI interview you. It's the habit that keeps AI-built projects from turning into a mess. Try skills in your coding agent: reusable, step-by-step guides that work across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. Get help from real people: a live build session, office hours, and a live project review. Win a share of $2,500. First place takes $1,250 plus a feature in the Devpost newsletter and on Devpost's socials. Everyone who submits an eligible project gets a Devpost Learn badge. Get started You'll need Node.js and Git installed, a coding agent that supports skills, and an empty folder for your project. In your empty project folder, run npx skills add challengepost/learn-ai-basics --all -y Open your coding agent in that folder and say "run 1-start." It takes it from there. Join the Devpost Discord for questions, office hours, and other builders' projects. Register for the Live Build Session , Thursday, Oct 1 at 1:00 pm ET, where we run the whole process start to finish. Recorded if you can't make it. RSVP for Cup of Joe office hours: Tuesday, Oct 6 and Tuesday, Oct 13 , 3:00 pm ET, in Discord voice. Bring your project and your questions, and get live feedback from Joe and other builders. Just drop in, no Zoom needed. Register for Will It Ship , Thursday, Oct 22 at 3:00 pm ET. A live review of about five submissions against the judging criteria, before the deadline, so you can still act on what you hear. Submit early to the Devpost Discord's Build with AI Basics forum if you want yours in the mix. Stuck? Ask in Discord or come to Cup of Joe office hours (Tuesdays Oct 6 and Oct 13 , 3:00 pm ET, Discord voice). Setup help and all event details are on the Resources tab. What to build A new app, built with the Devpost Learn Skill Pack. The skills will help you find an idea if you don't have one, and cut it down if you have too much of one. Three requirements, all checked at submission: New project, started from an empty folder during the submission period. Old ideas are fine, old code is not. Built with the skills. Run them in your coding agent. Planning docs in the repo. Your public repository must include the scope.md, prd.md, and spec.md files the skills generate.

title: BOSS Battle
description: Bitshala builds and teaches Bitcoin Open Source Software — that's the "BOSS" in our name, and also the joke behind this one. Between cohort-based learning on Bitcoin's protocol and privacy stack, and the invite-only BOSS Summit that gathers India's sharpest Bitcoin OSS builders twice a year, we've mostly kept things small and deep. BOSS Battle flips that: it's virtual, it's open, and it's a hackathon instead of a summit. You don't need a GitHub history full of BIPs to show up. Beginners get workshops, mentors, and a community that answers questions instead of gatekeeping them. Experienced builders get a chance to finally prototype the thing they've been meaning to build, surrounded by people who actually get it.
